newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Switkowksi resigns as Optus chief executive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Switkowksi resigns as Optus chief executive.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd, Australia's second biggest telecommunications carrier, said on Friday that chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski had tendered his resignation and would be replaced by Peter Howell-Davies.
The company also said chairman Russell Fynmore had resigned.
Switkowski became chief executive about one year ago after a long career at Eastman Kodak Co, replacing Bob Mansfield.
His resignation had been mooted for a number of weeks.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday that the Optus board was unhappy with Switkowski's handling of some strategic issues, in particular the future of the pay-television unit Optus Vision.
The statement by Optus did not say why Switkowski had resigned but said one of Howell-Davies' first duties would be to focus on Optus Vision.

Optus Vision, which has about 185,000 subscribers, is involved in a fierce battle for market share with its main rival Foxtel, which is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Telstra. Foxtel has about 140,000 subscribers.
The two pay-tv groups, and the struggling third-ranked Australis Media Ltd, are estimated to have lost a combined A$1.5 billion.
Foxtel has committed to spending A$3 billion on cabling as many households as possible in Australian cities.
Australis said earlier on Friday that it was involved in possible merger talks with either Optus Vision or Foxtel.

A merger of Foxtel and Australis was blocked by anti-monopolies regulators in late 1995 but Australis sources said they were more confident now that a merger would not be blocked due to upcoming telecoms deregulation.
